examples.question_text:
Find the interquartile range in each case.
a. $Q_1 = 13.6$ minutes and $Q_3 = 28.9$ minutes.
b. Temperatures ($^{\circ}\text{C}$): $7, -4, 12, 1, -8, 4, 9, -1, 15$.
c. Times (minutes), in ascending order: $5.2, 7.4, 9.6, 12.3, 14.8, 17.5, 21.1, 24.6$.
examples.solution_text:
a. $\begin{aligned}\text{IQR} &= Q_3-Q_1\\&=28.9-13.6\\&=15.3\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$
b. In ascending order: $-8, -4, -1, 1, 4, 7, 9, 12, 15$.
Leave out the single middle value, $4$.
Lower half: $-8, -4, -1, 1$; upper half: $7, 9, 12, 15$.
$Q_1 = \frac{-4+(-1)}{2} = -2.5$
$Q_3 = \frac{9+12}{2} = 10.5$
$\begin{aligned}\text{IQR} &=10.5-(-2.5)\\&=13^{\circ}\text{C}\end{aligned}$
c. Lower half: $5.2, 7.4, 9.6, 12.3$; upper half: $14.8, 17.5, 21.1, 24.6$.
$Q_1 = \frac{7.4+9.6}{2} = 8.5$
$Q_3 = \frac{17.5+21.1}{2} = 19.3$
$\begin{aligned}\text{IQR} &=19.3-8.5\\&=10.8\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Two groups record travel times (minutes).
Group A: $8, 11, 13, 16, 18, 20, 22, 43$.
Group B: $6, 10, 14, 19, 24, 28, 32, 37$.
Find each range and IQR. Which group's middle $50\%$ of times is more consistent? Explain why range and IQR give different comparisons.
examples.solution_text:
Group A: $\text{Range} = 43 - 8 = 35$ minutes.
$Q_1 = \frac{11+13}{2} = 12$, $Q_3 = \frac{20+22}{2} = 21$.
$\text{IQR}_A = 21 - 12 = 9$ minutes.
Group B: $\text{Range} = 37 - 6 = 31$ minutes.
$Q_1 = \frac{10+14}{2} = 12$, $Q_3 = \frac{28+32}{2} = 30$.
$\text{IQR}_B = 30 - 12 = 18$ minutes.
Group A has the smaller IQR, so its middle $50\%$ of times is more consistent. The extreme time of $43$ minutes extends Group A's upper extreme, but each range depends on both endpoints: $43-8=35$ minutes for Group A and $37-6=31$ minutes for Group B. Range uses the two extremes; IQR uses the middle half.

examples.question_text:
The ordered scores are $4, 7, 11, 15, 18, 22, 27, 31$.
a. Find the range and IQR.
b. Add a score of $49$. Find the new range and IQR. Explain whether the IQR is unchanged.
examples.solution_text:
a. $\text{Range} = 31 - 4 = 27$.
Lower half: $4, 7, 11, 15$; upper half: $18, 22, 27, 31$.
$Q_1 = \frac{7+11}{2} = 9$, $Q_3 = \frac{22+27}{2} = 24.5$.
$\text{IQR} = 24.5 - 9 = 15.5$.
b. New ordered scores: $4, 7, 11, 15, 18, 22, 27, 31, 49$.
$\text{Range} = 49 - 4 = 45$.
Leave out the single middle score, $18$.
Lower half: $4, 7, 11, 15$; upper half: $22, 27, 31, 49$.
$Q_1 = 9$, $Q_3 = \frac{27+31}{2} = 29$.
$\text{IQR} = 29 - 9 = 20$.
The range increases by $18$ and the IQR increases by $4.5$. Adding a score changes the quartile positions, so the IQR need not stay unchanged.

examples.question_text:
a. $Q_1 = 16.8$ minutes and the IQR is $12.7$ minutes. Find $Q_3$.
b. $Q_3 = 34.6$ minutes and the IQR is $18.3$ minutes. Find $Q_1$.
c. The ordered scores are $8, 13, x, 24, 29, 35, 42, 48$. Their IQR is $21$. Find $x$.
examples.solution_text:
a. $\begin{aligned}\text{IQR} &= Q_3-Q_1\\12.7 &= Q_3-16.8\\Q_3 &=29.5\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$
b. $\begin{aligned}18.3 &=34.6-Q_1\\Q_1 &=34.6-18.3\\&=16.3\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$
c. Lower half: $8, 13, x, 24$; upper half: $29, 35, 42, 48$.
$Q_1 = \frac{13+x}{2}$, $Q_3 = \frac{35+42}{2} = 38.5$.
$\begin{aligned}21 &=38.5-\frac{13+x}{2}\\\frac{13+x}{2} &=17.5\\13+x &=35\\x &=22\end{aligned}$
$13 < 22 < 24$, so the scores remain in order.

examples.question_text:
Find the interquartile range of each ordered dataset.
a. $6, 9, 12, 16, 21, 25, 30$.
b. $3, 5, 8, 11, 14, 18, 23, 27, 32, 36$.
examples.solution_text:
a. Leave out the single middle value, $16$.
Lower half: $6, 9, 12$; upper half: $21, 25, 30$.
Each half has three values, so its median is the middle value.
$Q_1=9$, $Q_3=25$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{IQR} &=Q_3-Q_1\\&=25-9\\&=16\end{aligned}$
b. Split the ten values into two halves.
Lower half: $3, 5, 8, 11, 14$; upper half: $18, 23, 27, 32, 36$.
Each half has five values, so its median is the middle value.
$Q_1=8$, $Q_3=27$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{IQR} &=Q_3-Q_1\\&=27-8\\&=19\end{aligned}$
